questions_for_integrator: Does the 4 cm sensor span give a usable signal on the tightest bend, or do outer sensors saturate or drop out?
Is the sensor forward offset (5 cm) helping or causing lag and oscillation?
Is the wheel track and mass giving enough turn authority without wheel slip at the chosen base speed?

intent: Establish a baseline geometry that is evenly spread, forward-looking and mid-range in every parameter. Five 12 mm sensors at 10 mm spacing, placed 5 cm ahead of the axle, give a smooth, well-resolved line-position signal for the Integrator, and the mid-range wheel track, radius, body and mass keep the dynamics predictable. I expect a complete run on the development tracks with few line-loss events. The Integrator's feedback should show whether the sensor spread gives enough signal at the bends and whether the forward offset causes too much lag.
learning: No prior race data. Next iteration, use the Integrator's feedback and the first race's telemetry to decide whether to widen or narrow the sensor span, move the sensors forward or back, and change wheel track or mass. Test one geometry change at a time where possible.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry or integration feedback yet, so this proposal rests on design priors from the contract rather than evidence. The main constraints are: the course must be covered in under 3 s (about 1.5 m/s average), the run ends if the robot leaves the line by more than max(0.06 m, tape_half_width + body_width/4), and line loss is costly in the score. Five sensors at 12 mm footprint and 10 mm spacing (x = -0.02 to +0.02) cover about 4 cm across the line, so the line stays visible through moderate lateral error and the signal stays smooth. Sensors sit 5 cm ahead of the axle so the controller sees the line before the wheels reach it, which reduces lag at bends. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a moderate turn authority (turn rate is set by the wheel speed difference over the track) without making the yaw inertia too large. Body width 0.12 m keeps the off-track limit at 0.06 m, since the body term (0.0125 + 0.03 m) is below that floor. Mass 0.8 kg is mid-range, which should give reasonable acceleration from the 7.4 V battery without much wheel slip. I expect this to complete the oval and s-bend tracks; slalom is the most uncertain because of the sharper alternating bends.
